title: Robust Reasoning as a Symmetry-Protected Topological Phase

While the formal microscopic derivation is detailed in the Methods, here we outline the physical principles governing this emergence. Causality as Chirality. The fundamental constraint of logical inference is causality: information flows strictly from t → t + 1 t\to t+1 . In the language of field theory [ 34 ] , this unidirectional flow explicitly breaks Time-Reversal ( 𝒯 \mathcal{T} ) symmetry, as the operation t → − t t\to-t would map forward-propagating modes (“right-movers”) to non-existent backward-propagating ones. In the continuum limit, this renders the neural hidden state an effective chiral spinor field. We emphasize that this identification is an effective description of the signal propagation modes, where the “chirality” captures the irreversible arrow of inference. It is a standard result in quantum field theory that coupling a gauge field to chiral fermions in ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) dimensions results in a chiral anomaly—a breakdown of gauge invariance due to the non-conservation of the chiral current. Anomaly Cancellation via Topology. To restore consistency, the effective action must be augmented by a topological counter-term: the Wess-Zumino (WZ) term [ 35 , 36 ] . Physically, this term implies that the local transition h t → h t + 1 h_{t}\to h_{t+1} cannot be treated as a free vector update; it is constrained by the global topology of the group manifold extended into a virtual ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) -dimensional bulk.
